terminal delight · tactical rework · workshop 1 · 2026-10-19

Tactical

Field folded into Tactical tonight, in pull request 1029. What Tactical still lacks is a skin of its own and the DIN type you asked for. This page tries both before any code is written: a skin that borrows XCOM 2's panels and Fallout 4's Pip-Boy selection, and takes its colours from whatever palette is on.

workshop · nothing built difficulty 6 / 10 fonts: all SIL OFL, embedded fold merged · PR 1029 issue 990 · DIN 1451

Recommendation

D-DIN Condensed Bold for names and headings, IBM Plex Mono for every number, and the terminal grid left alone. A new tactical skin draws cut panels, chevron titles, segmented gauges and a Pip-Boy selection bar in the active palette's colours, and the Tactical design asks for it the way Deco asks for its own skin. Four of the nine marks already have a key in the skin file; five need one.

01What the fold left

02The type

DIN 1451 is German road-sign lettering, drawn on a grid from one stroke width, in a medium and a condensed cut. D-DIN is Datto's open-licence DIN, and it ships both.

03The interface

TD's window, with the rows from the Chalk review capture, redrawn in the skin. Try the type on it.

heading + data grid

04Where it has to reach

A skin is a TOML file in app/skins/: ink recipes from the palette, size metrics and shape switches. Tactical would be the fifth, and the Tactical design would name it with skin = "tactical", as Deco does.

05Yours

1 · Heading face

Six directions in figure 3.

Recommendation: A. D-DIN Condensed Bold for headings, D-DIN Bold for names in the tree. OFL, so it bundles the way Caveat does.

2 · Number and readout face

Percentages, counters, paths, the zoom level.

Recommendation: IBM Plex Mono. Share Tech Mono is more Pip-Boy, but its zero and capital O are close at 11 px.

3 · Terminal grid font

Field and Tactical both set the grid in JetBrains Mono today. Try the other two with the grid chips above figure 5.

Recommendation: leave it. The grid belongs to the programs in it, and issue 990 warns against bending it to a signage face.

4 · Tactical's dials

The fold kept Tactical's glow 0.78 and bezel 0.98, the strongest in the set. Figure 9 is the argument for less.

Recommendation: the quieter amber column in figure 1, and the design file names its skin with skin = "tactical".

5 · The marks

The nine pins in figure 6. Five of them add a key to the skin file (figure 10).

Recommendation: all nine, built as skin keys any skin can use. No full-screen phosphor tint (figure 9, left).

6 · What comes next

Difficulty 6 / 10, the same as Chalk: one skin across the surfaces in figure 11, five new skin keys, and a bundled font.

Recommendation: your notes become one plan page in docs/plans/tactical-skin/, then a native build photographed on every surface in figure 11. Whether to reach the orange rows now, or for every skin at once, is yours.

06 Behind this

What each picture is drawn from

their design · the code · mine

From the code. Figure 1's dials come from the two theme files as they stood before pull request 1029 removed Field. Figures 10 and 11 come from a read of app/src/skin.rs and its callers on main at d9912a6c, with file and line for each row in docs/skins/SURFACES.md, plus the Chalk records in docs/plans/chalk-flower/. The strings and rows in figures 5–7 are the ones in the Chalk review capture (reports/2026-10-20-chalk-marker-evidence/current.webp).

From the sources you sent. The XCOM 2 and Fallout 4 screenshots, the FallUI page, the DIN reference sheet, the ChatGPT table of combinations, and parker-job's stylesheet (app.css: --grn #00ff9c, --army #8db43c, --orange #ff9d2e, the 44 px grid).

Mine. Every mark's placement, the amber dial values, the selection colour, the sticky-note-as-orders tag, and which game each mark is credited to. None of this has been rendered by TD. gpui's text shaping and the CRT warp will change how it feels.

The one measured number. Figure 4: advance widths summed with fontTools from each font file at 14 px, bold or semibold instance, no letter-spacing, no kerning. Kerning would narrow every face by a few pixels and leave the order unchanged.

The ChatGPT conversation could not be fetched; the share page renders client-side. The table in your screenshot is what this page used.

all embedded in this file, Latin subset, woff2

OFL allows bundling in the binary, which is how TD already ships Caveat and News Cycle (app/assets/fonts/, loaded with include_bytes! in main.rs). The reserved-name clause means a modified D-DIN could not be shipped under that name; bundling it unmodified is fine. Linotype's DIN 1451 is commercial and was not considered.
